column6: Michelet named as part of the political-narrative tradition Annales opposed; Febvre claimed Michelet as a forerunner. Replaced with Seignobos, the actual French target.
On a 13.8-billion-year calendar, agriculture, cities and industry fall in the final ~30 seconds, not "final minutes"; changed to "final seconds".

Dualism "formalized by Descartes" overstated the attribution (soul-body dualism predates him, e.g. Plato); now "given its classic modern form by Descartes". Explainer has the same simplification (left).
TOC order (environment, collective destinies, events) and "crests of foam" quote verified.
Not fixed (old Explainer): first trial usually dated 1584 (denounced 1583); left as uncertain.
Moore's Social Origins cases are England, France, the US, China, Japan and India; Germany was not a main case and the US and China were missing.
Same Moore case list error in the Explainer; corrected.
French and Russian Revolutions linked by Atlantic abolitionism and Enlightenment print culture is incoherent; changed to French and Haitian Revolutions.
Not fixed (old q:4:explanation): perlocutionary effect glossed as "intended impact"; in Austin it is the effect actually produced.
Says little ... about social organization overstated; ancient DNA has reconstructed kinship and residence patterns. Now "gives only partial clues about social organization, such as kinship".
Answer said the institutions "occupied most of human existence before them" (reversed sense); now says humans lived most of their existence before these institutions appeared.
Vico did not restore providence is wrong; the New Science gives providence a central role working through human institutions. Answer key unaffected.
Not fixed (old q:0/q:2 explanations, Explainer): "India shaped Britain as much as Britain shaped India" is a contested claim stated as settled.
Style only: banned word "landscapes" changed to "lands".
Not fixed (old): Weber presented as plainly idealist; Weber himself disclaimed a one-sided spiritualist explanation.
D&P opening (Damiens 1757 vs. Faucher timetable) verified.
Not fixed (old Explainer/q:0): act-to-identity shift for sodomy/homosexuality stated as settled fact; it is Foucault's contested thesis.
Not fixed (old Core Idea): says Foucauldian genealogy traces concepts "back to their problematic foundations", which contradicts its anti-origin stance.
Family reconstitution credited to the Cambridge Group; it was pioneered by Louis Henry (with Fleury) in France and developed in England by the Cambridge Group.
